note: Adapted from the species description in Chhotani (1997), originally in English; the alate is recorded as unknown, only the soldier and worker being described; the original also appends a table of selected measurements, whose headings and tabulated data are not reproduced while measurements given in the text are transcribed as they stand; the upper limit of worker postclypeus width appears as '0..49' in the original, the separator being damaged, and is therefore not recorded; synonymy lists, literature citations, figure numbers and distribution records are omitted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule straw yellow, antennae, labrum and legs nearly white, abdominal tergites and sternites transparent. Head sparsely pilose, the frontal projection with several long setae; body rather densely pilose, the setae of the syntypes appearing to have been lost. Body length 4.5–4.8 mm. Head capsule subrectangular, broader anteriorly (length including mandibles 2.60–2.65 mm, length to mandible base 1.15–1.18 mm, to apex of frontal projection 1.20 mm, maximum width 0.90–0.93 mm); frontal projection broadly rounded in dorsal view, slightly raised in lateral view with anterior margin nearly straight (length 0.08–0.10 mm). Fontanelle situated below the frontal projection, frontal gland large. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 about as long as segment 2, segment 4 shortest. Anterior margin of labrum deeply incurved (length 0.25–0.28 mm, width 0.20–0.25 mm). Mandibles slender and rod-like, much longer than head (left mandible length 1.45–1.48 mm, right mandible length 1.43 mm, left mandible length/head length 1.28). Postmentum rod-like, waist very weakly constricted.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule milky white, thorax, legs and antennae nearly white, abdomen transparent; head and body rather densely pilose. Body length 3.4–3.5 mm. Head subcircular (length to apex of labrum 1.0 mm, length to mandible base 0.65 mm, maximum width 0.80–0.89 mm). Fontanelle plate small, oval. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 shorter than segment 2, segment 4 shortest. Postclypeus inflated (length 0.18 mm). Dorsal spur of the fore tibia not evident in the syntypes examined.
